findings.description: The new code calls .strip() on the prompt text, which removes trailing whitespace as well as the ANSI codes, so a prompt such as "Name: " is passed to input() as "Name:".
findings.rationale: Trigger: prompt("Name: ") or confirm("Continue? ") runs while the destination stream is not a TTY, so should_strip_ansi returns true even if the text has no ANSI codes. Mechanism: strip_ansi(text).strip() drops the trailing space, so the prompt is shown with no separator before the cursor. Impact: non-TTY and CliRunner output changes for every prompt that ends in a space, and tests that compare that output will fail. Only the ANSI removal was intended, so the whitespace trim is an unintended side effect.
